question: Should DeepSeek browser-only support retain legacy platform tokens from provider config for upgrade compatibility, or enforce an ephemeral-only Chrome-session model?
rationale: The branch intentionally preserves and rehydrates a sensitive legacy session token while automatic imports remain in memory; tests cannot decide whether that persistence boundary matches the repository's desired privacy and compatibility contract.

options.title: Preserve legacy compatibility
options.body: Accept read-only legacy token support, prohibit writing newly imported tokens, document the storage boundary, and require live upgrade/account-isolation proof.

options.title: Migrate to ephemeral sessions
options.body: Remove stored legacy platform tokens during normalization and require signed-in Chrome discovery, with clear upgrade guidance for affected users.

options.title: Narrow the feature
options.body: Keep API-key balance plus optional detailed usage but defer browser-only balance until the credential model is settled.

recommendation.title: Preserve legacy compatibility
recommendation.body: Accept read-only legacy token support, prohibit writing newly imported tokens, document the storage boundary, and require live upgrade/account-isolation proof.

likelyOwner.reason: As repository owner and release integrator for the existing DeepSeek feature, steipete is the strongest available owner for the privacy-versus-upgrade compatibility choice.
